_note: Verified against live api.enigma.com 2026-05-29. The two structural rules below cause most HTTP 400s; field-name fixes follow.

search_is_a_union.note: Query.search returns [SearchUnion] (Brand|OperatingLocation|LegalEntity|Person|Address). No edges/node/first on search itself.

nested_fields_are_connections.note: names, websites, addresses, operatingLocations, legalEntities, cardTransactions, industries, roles, tins, registeredEntities, registrations, persons, etc. are all Relay *Connection types.

conditions_types.Conditions: searchInput.conditions and node-level aggregator conditions. Fields: filter, orderBy, limit, pageToken.
conditions_types.ConnectionConditions: connection args (operatingLocations(conditions:), cardTransactions(conditions:), ...). Fields: filter, orderBy ONLY (no limit). Declare connection-condition variables as ConnectionConditions.

Address.correct: streetAddress1, streetAddress2, city, state, zip, fullAddress, county, msa, csa, latitude, longitude, country
Address.note: OUTPUT Address type uses streetAddress1/zip. INPUT AddressInput uses street1/postalCode. Do not cross them.

Website.note: The field is 'website', NOT 'url'. Also: subdomain, domain, topLevelDomain, path.

Role.note: Role has NO names/roleType/fullName. Reach a person's name via Role.legalEntities -> persons -> names { edges { node { firstName lastName fullName } } }.

PersonName.note: Person.names is a connection of PersonName. Person has no direct fullName scalar.

BrandCardTransaction.correct: quantityType, period, projectedQuantity, platformBrandId, periodStartDate, periodEndDate
BrandCardTransaction.note: Brand level has projectedQuantity only (NO rawQuantity). 'rank' is a valid FILTER path but not a returned scalar. Filter platformBrandId IS_NULL at brand level.

OperatingLocationCardTransaction.correct: quantityType, period, rawQuantity, projectedQuantity, periodStartDate, periodEndDate
OperatingLocationCardTransaction.note: OL level has BOTH rawQuantity and projectedQuantity, and NO platformBrandId. Do not filter platformBrandId at OL level.

RegisteredEntity.note: Both formationYear (Int) and formationDate (Date) exist. fileNumber/status/jurisdiction live on the nested 'registrations' connection.

Registration.correct: status, subStatus, statusDetail, registrationType, registrationState, jurisdictionType, homeJurisdictionState, registeredName, fileNumber, issueDate, expirationDate
Registration.note: Status field is 'status' (NOT 'registrationStatus'). Jurisdiction is 'registrationState'/'jurisdictionType'/'homeJurisdictionState' (no field named 'jurisdiction'). Registration.roles holds officers/agents.

WatchlistEntry.note: Only 'watchlistName' is present on the node from isFlaggedByWatchlistEntries; there is no 'entityName'.

LegalEntityBankruptcy.correct: caseNumber, filingDate, chapterType, debtorName, trustee, judge, petition, entryDate, dateConverted, dateDismissed, dateTerminated, debtorDischargedDate, planConfirmedDate

LegalEntity.persons.note: Populatedness is type-dependent: person-type LE nodes (reached via OL roles, or via registration roles) return populated persons; business-type LE nodes usually return empty. For officers traverse registeredEntities -> registrations -> roles -> legalEntities -> persons.

common_mistakes.mistake: declaring a connection-conditions variable as Conditions
prompt with entityType OPERATING_LOCATION on search
common_mistakes.correction: prompt search requires entityType BRAND (OL prompt only works for aggregate/export)
aggregate requires entityType OPERATING_LOCATION; use conditions.filter not prompt for accurate counts
Not supported. Use aggregate / node-level count, or pageInfo.hasNextPage.

common_mistakes.mistake: HAS with a scalar leaf path
common_mistakes.correction: HAS operand must be a path to a connection/type, e.g. HAS:['operatingLocations.phoneNumbers']

introspection_template:
python3 << 'PYEOF'
import json, urllib.request, os
query = '{ __type(name: "TYPE_NAME_HERE") { fields { name type { name kind ofType { name } } } } }'
payload = json.dumps({'query': query})
req = urllib.request.Request('https://api.enigma.com/graphql', data=payload.encode(),
    headers={'content-type': 'application/json', 'x-api-key': os.environ['ENIGMA_API_KEY']})
data = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req).read())
for f in data['data']['__type']['fields']:
    print(f"{f['name']}: {f['type']['name'] or f['type']['kind']}")
PYEOF
